author: reek
body: The process table already copies the parent's capability MASK into a child at spawn, and if the scope did not travel beside it the whole ring would have a door in it: a program scoped to "OK" could spawn a child whose scope cell was zero, and a zero scope is an unscoped grant -- the empty prefix admits every path. The child would inherit the authority to touch the disk and lose the limit on what it may name, which is a capability amplification dressed as a fork.

author: reek
body: So the parent here is scoped to "OK" and does nothing itself. The child attempts BOTH writes and reports both answers in one number: ten if the in-scope write landed, plus one if the out-of-scope write landed.

author: reek
body: Both effectful calls sit in tail or argument position rather than in a let: a let bound to a value with a concrete effect row is CDX2033, and poke-byte is itself effectful, so binding the report would be rejected before the write ever mattered. Nest, do not bind.
